public_rationale: The warning about general intelligence holds: METR describes a restricted benchmark whose tasks differ from ordinary work. The word only is too strong under a literal reading of software development. METR explicitly includes machine learning and cybersecurity. If Marcus intended software development as shorthand for that whole technical cluster, the disagreement is largely terminological; that interpretation is flagged.
limitations: The boundary between software development, ML engineering, and cybersecurity is not sharp.
The documentation read is the September 8 version; its update history identifies May 8 as the relevant graph update.
A restricted benchmark may still provide indirect evidence about broader capabilities.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The METR time-horizon graph pertains only to software-development tasks, not general intelligence.

statement.excerpt: The graph pertains only to software-development tasks. Not general intelligence.

our_interpretation: Assess the task coverage and interpretation of the graph available when Marcus posted.
Use the May 8–10 graph snapshot, the latest published update before the post.
Read software development ordinarily as developing and maintaining software. Do not silently expand only to encompass every technical task performed through a computer.
Read not general intelligence as a limitation on what this benchmark directly measures, not as a claim that its results contain no information about broader capabilities.
criteria.support_condition: The task inventory is confined to software development, and the graph does not directly establish general intelligence.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The inventory includes materially distinct task domains, contradicting only software development; evidence of broad, representative capability measurement would separately contradict the second clause.
